parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing criminalisation: civilian trans expression is lawful, and the military statute does not reach visitors. Rule-of-law mitigates strongly — courts have repeatedly ruled FOR trans people (police restroom advice unlawful with state compensation, surgery mandate struck down, LGR expanded), and police deployed heavily to protect Pride. Positives include established, visitor-friendly capital LGBTQ neighbourhoods and free media/civil society. Offsetting: organised violent conservative opposition (one Pride attacked, alleged police inaction), no comprehensive anti-discrimination law leaving visitors thin formal recourse, and an institutional health gap (ministry refusing hospitalisation guidelines) that makes emergency-care treatment an open question, not a documented exposure. The pervasive discrimination survey and school-restroom findings are resident-sphere. Military criminalisation and the 2020 outing incident are tangential or dated. Net: acceptance with working remedies but real friction and institutional gaps.
